items.title: Ed Polcer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: Wynton, who I disagree with on a lot of points wrote this great article

ctx.x: Do you feel that there needs to be more emphasis on the audience for jazz? Maybe I’m spouting my own feelings here.

Well let me say this. My son is majoring, just decided to major in jazz performance at the University of Michigan. And he already knows the business side from watching me in action. And already I’m feeling that he could get, there should be more given to him other than just the pure music part of it. Is that what you’re trying to say? Well the business side of it. The personality, all this kind of stuff. It was a great article, Wynton, who I disagree with on a lot of points wrote this great article, it was in…

Well I guess I look at all the players coming out of the jazz programs and many of them are really, really good. I’m wondering where they’re going to go with it if there’s no audience for it, and if there’s something we could do, and I guess what you’re doing here with the Swing Street —
